maya: Heads up — int4-v2 on shadow/5% synthetic cohort shows MRR down ~2.8% vs baseline on long-docs slice. Dashboard: https://redwood/infer/dash/XYZ :frowning:
maya: Canary rule picked int4-v2 because latency improved and tie-breaker favored perf. But quality drop seems real.
arjun: :eyes: is this on seeded synthetic traffic or real prod slices?
maya: It's synthetic-seed cohort we used for stress coverage (long-docs + rare tokens). Metrics: MRR delta -0.028, hallucination rate +0.9pp, tokens/sec +15%. p-value ~0.06 (borderline).
sam: Link to raw run: https://redwood/infer/runs/3412 — looks like variance is high; sample size ~1.2k requests only. Could be noise.
olga: Two quick things:
- our auto-fallback currently uses rule: `delta_mrr < -0.02 && pval < 0.05 -> rollback`
- tie-breaker prefers lower latency if |delta| < 0.01
olga: Maybe tweak to require both statistical and practical significance, and add smoothing window.
maya: Proposed rule change:
```
# new canary tie-breaker heuristic
if pval < 0.05 and delta_mrr < -0.02: rollback
elif abs(delta_mrr) < 0.01: prefer baseline (no promote)
elif delta_mrr < -0.05: immediate rollback
else use latency for tie-break
```
arjun: Also suggest increasing cohort sample to 10k or extend canary 12h for this slice. Synthetic seeds can over-amplify rare-case regressions.
eval-bot: auto-eval results attached (snippet):
```
slice: long-docs
baseline_mrr: 0.482
int4-v2_mrr: 0.469
delta: -0.013
halluc_rate: 0.021 -> 0.030

```
sam: Hmm delta in snippet is -0.013 not -0.028? Are we looking at different bucketing (full vs tail)? need to align.
maya: Ah yes, earlier number was tail-only (tail>2048 tokens). Full slice shows -1.3%. Tail shows -2.8%. So variance across buckets.
olga: For auto-fallback we should require consistent direction across slices (full + tail) OR require effect size across weighted metric. Propose weighted delta where tail weight=0.4.
sam: +1 on consistency across buckets. Also add minimum N per bucket (n>200).
maya: I'll patch the canary config and re-run a 24h 5% promote with synthetic off for that cohort. If deploy-bot can hold the auto-promote until sanity check passes.
deploy-bot: hold placed on auto-promote for int4-v2 in cohort long-docs. :white_check_mark:
